equip.hero_lede: A breaker that trips is telling you something, and it is not always that the breaker is bad. We diagnose the circuit before anyone quotes a panel — then, because we hold current City of Chicago registration, we pull and close the permit when the work needs one.
equip.issue_options: Breaker keeps tripping||Breaker will not reset||Burning smell or heat at the panel||Panel is full / need a new circuit||Fuse box or obsolete panel||Quote only
equip.types_lede: Everything installed across Chicago's housing stock, from a 15A branch circuit in a bungalow to a panel an insurer has flagged.

equip.types_footnote: We also handle everything around the panel on the same visit — junction boxes, dead circuits, flickering, warm outlets, buzzing panels, and the load calculation behind a new circuit.
equip.brands_lede: Ten names cover most of what we meet on this work across Chicago.
equip.brands_note: Federal Pacific Stab-Lok and Zinsco panels have a documented history of breakers failing to trip under fault. If you have one, replacement is the honest recommendation and we will say so in writing.
equip.why_heading: Why Highlights Chicago for Breaker Work
equip.why_lede: Six reasons specific to this trade in this city, not the licensed-and-insured line every contractor runs.
equip.why: We hold the registration that closes the permit::ECC96456 and ECC94521 in Chicago, plus Evanston 18LICL-0250 and Palatine CON-006592-2024, all verified active July 2026. Illinois licenses no electricians at state level; only a registered contractor may pull the permit.||1,213 permits on public record since 2012::Ranked #73 of the 588 licensed electrical contractors pulling permits in Chicago — the top 13% by volume. Government-sourced, and not something a competitor can answer.||The person quoting is salaried, not commissioned::In-house master electricians in named crews — Boz, Victor, Raul, Jimmy, Kaplan, Niki. Nobody is paid more for the bigger answer, so a breaker fault gets diagnosed as a breaker fault.||We still take the small job::Reviewers describe single breaker swaps handled quickly and priced fairly. Most Chicago electricians will not schedule that visit at all.||Chicago conduit is a baseline skill here::The City of Chicago Electrical Code requires metal raceway — NM cable is not permitted across essentially the whole city. Routine for our crews, a genuine barrier for contractors from outside.||Panel work is our highest-volume category::163 panel jobs and 162 200-amp upgrades in our own permit record, against 5,219 panel permits citywide in 24 months.
equip.feature_desc: Every service we offer in the Panels, Circuits & Protection cluster across Chicago.
equip.other_services: Whole-House Generator Installation::A standby generator is not an appliance you plug in — it is a permitted electrical project with a transfer switch, a loa.::https://www.highlightschicago.com/services/generator-installation/||Solar Panel Installation & Service::Solar is the second-highest-volume permitted electrical category in Chicago — 4,033 permits in 24 months.::https://www.highlightschicago.com/services/solar-panel-installation/||Ceiling Fan Installation::A ceiling fan looks like a small job until the box in the ceiling turns out to be a lighting box that was never rated to.::https://www.highlightschicago.com/services/ceiling-fan-installation/||Generator Repair & Maintenance::A standby generator that has not been exercised is a very expensive ornament.::https://www.highlightschicago.com/services/generator-repair/
equip.pricing_lede: We do not publish a flat-rate price book, because the same symptom can be a free reset or a service upgrade. What we can publish is the citywide permit data and exactly what drives the number.

equip.pricing_col_2: What drives the price / reported median
equip.pricing_rows: Breaker keeps tripping::Diagnosis time; whether the fault is the breaker, the circuit or the load::No||Single breaker replacement::Breaker type — standard, GFCI, AFCI or dual-function — and panel compatibility::No||Adding a circuit::Available spaces, load calculation, conduit run through masonry::Usually||Electrical panel, any (5,219 permits)::$15,906 median reported construction value::Yes||200A service upgrade (2,863 permits)::$4,700 median reported construction value::Yes||Federal Pacific / Zinsco swap::Panel size and location; occasionally an insurer deadline::Yes
equip.pricing_note: Permit medians are reported construction value for whole projects, not contractor quotes. Free estimates; written scope before work starts.
equip.faqs: My breaker keeps tripping. Does it need replacing?::Usually not. A breaker that trips is doing its job — something on that circuit is drawing more current than it should, or there is a fault. Replacing the breaker without finding the cause removes the warning and leaves the problem.||Do I need a permit for breaker work in Chicago?::Not for a repair or a like-for-like breaker replacement. You do for a panel replacement, a service upgrade, or in most cases adding a new circuit. We pull and close it in-house.||I have a Federal Pacific or Zinsco panel. Is it really a problem?::Yes, and it is one of the few cases where we recommend replacement without trying a repair first. Both have a documented history of breakers failing to trip under fault conditions.||Why can't you just add a breaker to my full panel?::Sometimes we can — tandem breakers fit certain panels. But spaces are not the real limit; service capacity is. That is why a load calculation comes before a price on any new circuit.||Will you come out for a single breaker?::Yes. It is the thing our reviewers mention most, because it is genuinely hard to find a Chicago electrician who will take one.
equip.cta_body: Free estimate, a written scope before we start, and a contractor registered to pull the permit if the work needs one.

page.guides:
Types of Homes in Chicago & Their Wiring::

What Chicago's building stock actually is

Cook County Assessor data makes the pattern unambiguous, and it explains most of what we find behind a cover plate.

83%

of properties in West Chicago township (Wicker Park, West Town, Ukrainian Village) predate 1940

1906

median year built in West Chicago township; 1908 in Lake View

265,194

masonry-walled properties citywide — why conduit through brick is routine here

306,261

properties with no central air — the load that gets added later

Why the age matters electrically

A building from 1906 was wired, if it was wired at all, for lighting. Everything since — the refrigerator, the window units, the home office, the induction range, the car — has been added to a service that was never designed for it. That is the single thread running through most Chicago electrical work.

Township by township

West Chicago is the oldest at 83% pre-1940 across 65,664 properties. Lake View follows at 71% across 23,046. Jefferson township — Portage Park, Jefferson Park, Irving Park — is younger at 60% pre-1940 but far larger at 112,923 properties, and its median year of 1927 puts most of it in the bungalow era. Rogers Park is the youngest of the north-side townships at a 1938 median.

What that means room by room

188,389 properties citywide are two-storey and 154,926 single-storey; 324,305 have full basements, which is where the panel usually lives and where access is usually straightforward. 107,336 properties have no garage at all — relevant the moment an EV charger enters the conversation. And 335,769 use a warm-air furnace against 98,849 on hot water or steam, which decides what kind of equipment circuits exist already.

||What Chicago's Permit Record Shows::

What the permit record shows

Chicago publishes every permit it issues. That makes contractor claims checkable, including ours.

1,213

Highlights Chicago permits on record, first in April 2012

Top 13%

#73 of the 588 licensed electrical contractors pulling Chicago permits over 24 months

$40,000

median project cost across 1,173 costed permits

29.7 days

average permit processing time on record

What we actually pull permits for

Our own job-type mix: 307 service or new service permits, 206 outlets and receptacles, 163 electrical panel, 162 200-amp service upgrades, 126 lighting, 117 100-amp service and 33 at 400 amp or larger. By permit route, 527 went through the Express Permit Program, 340 new construction and 325 renovation or alteration.

Where we work most

Ward 1 (129 permits), Ward 32 (85), Ward 26 (72), Ward 47 (68) and Ward 27 (63) lead our record — the north and northwest sides, consistent with a shop on N Lincoln Ave.

The citywide picture

Chicago issued 20,187 electrical permits in 24 months. Lighting leads at 9,748, outlets and receptacles at 9,306, service work at 6,672, panels at 5,219 and solar at 4,033. At the other end, rewires ran to 28 permits and ceiling fans to 3 — a useful corrective to any contractor telling you a whole-house rewire is routine.

One honest caveat

Permit values are the reported construction value of the whole project, which often includes trades other than ours. They are a good guide to the scale of a job and a poor guide to a contractor's revenue. We quote from scope, not from permit data.

||Chicago Neighbourhood & Suburb Guide::

Where we work, and what changes between areas

North Side — Lincoln Square, North Park, Albany Park, Ravenswood

Our home patch, minutes from the shop on N Lincoln Ave. Dense bungalow and two-flat stock; fuse boxes and 100A services still turn up regularly.

Lakefront — Uptown, Rogers Park, Lakeview

Lake View township is 71% pre-1940. Courtyard buildings and pre-war condo conversions, where metering and common-area circuits dominate.

Northwest — Logan Square, Wicker Park, Jefferson Park

West Chicago township is 83% pre-1940 — the oldest stock in the city. Knob-and-tube behind new drywall is the recurring surprise on rehab work.

Suburbs — Evanston and Palatine

Current registration in both (18LICL-0250 and CON-006592-2024), so we can pull permits there. Our DuPage registrations have lapsed and we do not sell permit-bearing work there.

Ward 1, 32, 26, 47 and 27 carry the largest share of our permit record, which is simply where a north-side shop ends up working.

||Whole-House Generator Installation — Detail::

Whole-House Generator Installation in Chicago — the practical detail

A standby generator is not an appliance you plug in — it is a permitted electrical project with a transfer switch, a load calculation and a gas connection behind it. Chicago issued 161 generator permits in the last 24 months. We pull ours in-house.

What drives the cost

Chicago publishes the reported construction value on every electrical permit. The medians below are the real distribution for this work across the city in the last 24 months — not our price list, but a far better anchor than a made-up range.

Before you book anyone

  • Do I need a permit for a generator in Chicago? — Yes. A standby generator with a transfer switch is permitted, inspected electrical work, and gas connection brings its own requirements. We pull and close the electrical permit under ECC96456.
  • What size generator do I actually need? — It depends on your connected load, not your square footage. Many Chicago homes are better served by an essential-circuits setup than a whole-house unit — same outcome in an outage, materially lower cost.
  • Whole-house or essential circuits? — Essential circuits backs up heat, refrigeration, sump and selected outlets. Whole-house backs up everything including central air. We price both so the decision is yours with numbers attached.
  • Can you work with my gas fitter? — Yes, and coordination is part of the schedule rather than something you have to project-manage between two trades.
  • How long does the install take? — Typically a small number of days on site once the permit and equipment are in hand. The lead time usually sits in equipment supply and permitting, not the labour.

Why the age matters electrically

A building from 1906 was wired, if it was wired at all, for lighting. Everything since — the refrigerator, the window units, the home office, the induction range, the car — has been added to a service that was never designed for it. Township by township

Rogers Park is the youngest of the north-side townships at a 1938 median.

What that means room by room

188,389 properties citywide are two-storey and 154,926 single-storey; 324,305 have full basements, which is where the panel usually lives and where access is usually straightforward. 107,336 properties have no garage at all — relevant the moment an EV charger enters the conversation. And 335,769 use a warm-air furnace against 98,849 on hot water or steam, which decides what kind of equipment circuits exist already.

||Solar Panel Installation & Service — Detail::

Solar Panel Installation & Service in Chicago — the practical detail

Solar is the second-highest-volume permitted electrical category in Chicago — 4,033 permits in 24 months. The array is the easy part; the interconnection, the panel capacity and the inspection sequence are where projects stall.

What drives the cost

Chicago publishes reported construction value on every permit. With 4,022 costed solar permits, this median is one of the most reliable figures in the whole dataset.

Before you book anyone

  • Do I need a panel upgrade before solar? — Often, yes. The array has to interconnect somewhere with capacity to spare. We assess the service first so the answer arrives before you sign, not during the install.
  • Do you repair solar you did not install? — Yes. Inverter faults, dead strings, monitoring dropouts and post-storm checks. It is a common call when the original installer has gone.
  • Is a permit required for solar in Chicago? — Yes, and solar is one of the highest-volume permitted categories in the city. We pull and close it in-house.
  • How long does interconnection take with ComEd? — Utility timelines vary and sit outside our control, which is exactly why we schedule around them rather than promising a date we cannot hold.
  • Does solar work on a Chicago flat roof? — Yes — ballasted or attached racking depending on the roof and the structure. Flat roofs are common here and are not an obstacle.

||Ceiling Fan Installation — Detail::

Ceiling Fan Installation in Chicago — the practical detail

A ceiling fan looks like a small job until the box in the ceiling turns out to be a lighting box that was never rated to carry a moving load — which, in a Chicago building of a certain age, it very often is.

What drives the cost

Almost no ceiling fan work is permitted in Chicago, so permit data tells you very little here. What drives the price is what is above the ceiling.

Before you book anyone

  • Can you install a fan where a light fixture is now? — Usually yes, and it is our most common fan job. The deciding factor is the box: a lighting box is not rated to carry a moving load, so we fit a fan-rated brace box.
  • Do I need a permit for a ceiling fan in Chicago? — Normally no. The city recorded only 3 permitted ceiling fan jobs in 24 months. If the work extends to a new circuit, that changes.
  • My ceiling is old lath and plaster. Is that a problem? — It is the normal situation in pre-war Chicago and not usually an obstacle. A brace box can generally be fitted from below without opening the ceiling.
  • Can I supply my own fan? — Yes, and most customers do. We install customer-supplied fans as standard.
  • Why is my existing fan wobbling? — Usually blade balance or a box that was never rated for the load. The second one matters — a fan on an unrated box is a genuine safety issue.

||Generator Repair & Maintenance — Detail::

Generator Repair & Maintenance in Chicago — the practical detail

A standby generator that has not been exercised is a very expensive ornament. Most of the failures we are called to are batteries, controllers and transfer switches — not engines — and most were visible months earlier.

What drives the cost

Most repairs are unpermitted service work, so permit data sets context rather than price. What drives the number is what actually failed.

Before you book anyone

  • My generator will not start. What is it usually? — In our experience, the battery far more often than the engine. Standby sets sit idle and batteries die quietly. That is the first thing we check, not the last.
  • It runs but the power stays off. Why? — That is a transfer switch or interlock fault, not an engine fault. The set is doing its job and the switch is not passing the load across.
  • Do you service generators you did not install? — Yes. It is one of our more common generator calls, particularly on houses that changed hands with the unit already there.
  • How often should a standby generator be serviced? — Annually as a baseline, plus regular self-exercise. A set that has never been exercised is the one that fails in the first outage.
  • Is generator repair permitted work in Chicago? — Usually not. Replacing the set or altering the transfer switch arrangement is — and we hold the registration to pull it.

Types of Homes in Chicago & Their Wiring::

What Chicago's building stock actually is

Cook County Assessor data makes the pattern unambiguous, and it explains most of what we find behind a cover plate.

Why the age matters electrically

A building from 1906 was wired, if it was wired at all, for lighting. Everything since — the refrigerator, the window units, the home office, the induction range, the car — has been added to a service that was never designed for it. That is the single thread running through most Chicago electrical work.

Township by township

West Chicago is the oldest at 83% pre-1940 across 65,664 properties. Lake View follows at 71% across 23,046. Jefferson township — Portage Park, Jefferson Park, Irving Park — is younger at 60% pre-1940 but far larger at 112,923 properties, and its median year of 1927 puts most of it in the bungalow era. Rogers Park is the youngest of the north-side townships at a 1938 median.

What that means room by room

188,389 properties citywide are two-storey and 154,926 single-storey; 324,305 have full basements, which is where the panel usually lives and where access is usually straightforward. 107,336 properties have no garage at all — relevant the moment an EV charger enters the conversation. And 335,769 use a warm-air furnace against 98,849 on hot water or steam, which decides what kind of equipment circuits exist already.

||Whole-House Surge Protection — Detail::

Whole-House Surge Protection in Chicago — the practical detail

A power strip protects one desk. A panel-mounted surge protective device protects the furnace board, the range, the HVAC condenser and everything else you cannot unplug — which, in a house full of electronics, is most of what a surge would actually cost you.

What drives the cost

Surge devices are usually installed alongside other panel work, which is exactly why the cost varies so much between doing it now and doing it later.

Before you book anyone

  • Is a whole-house surge protector worth it? — It depends on what you have behind the panel. Modern HVAC boards, induction ranges and home offices are the expensive casualties. If your house is full of them, the arithmetic is straightforward.
  • Does it replace power strips? — No — it layers with them. The panel device takes the large transient; point-of-use devices handle what gets past it.
  • Do I need a permit for a surge protector? — Usually not on its own. If it is fitted during a panel replacement or service upgrade, that work is permitted and we pull it.
  • Will it protect against a direct lightning strike? — No, and any contractor who says otherwise is overselling. It protects against transients, including the far more common ones from utility switching.
  • Can it be added to my existing panel? — Usually, provided there is space and the panel accepts a matched device. We check before quoting rather than after.

||GFCI Outlet Installation & Repair — Detail::

GFCI Outlet Installation & Repair in Chicago — the practical detail

A GFCI that trips constantly is usually right. A GFCI that will not reset is telling you something specific, and in Chicago's pre-war housing stock the answer is frequently an ungrounded two-wire circuit that no amount of swapping devices will fix.

What drives the cost

GFCI work is rarely permitted on its own — only 24 GFCI permits citywide in 24 months. Price follows circuit condition and access.

Before you book anyone

  • Why does my GFCI keep tripping? — Because it is detecting current going somewhere it should not — often moisture in an exterior or bathroom circuit, sometimes a failing appliance. A GFCI that trips repeatedly is doing its job and pointing at something.
  • My GFCI will not reset at all. What now? — Either there is a live fault on the circuit, the device has failed, or there is no power reaching it. Those are three different repairs, which is why diagnosis comes before a replacement device.
  • Can I have GFCI protection on an ungrounded circuit? — Yes, and in Chicago's pre-war stock it is a common and legitimate solution — with correct labelling, which is part of the job.
  • Where does Chicago require GFCI protection? — Kitchens, bathrooms, garages, unfinished basements, exteriors and near sinks generally. If you are selling, this is a routine inspection finding.
  • Do I need a permit to replace an outlet? — Not for a like-for-like replacement. Adding a new circuit is a different matter and usually is permitted.

||Garbage Disposal Installation & Wiring — Detail::

Garbage Disposal Installation & Wiring in Chicago — the practical detail

The plumbing half of a disposal is straightforward. The electrical half — a dedicated circuit, a correctly switched supply and a GFCI arrangement that satisfies an inspector — is the half that fails, and it is the half we do.

What drives the cost

Disposal circuits are rarely permitted alone; they usually sit inside kitchen work. Price follows whether a circuit already exists.

Before you book anyone

  • Do I need a dedicated circuit for a garbage disposal? — In practice, yes. Sharing with the dishwasher is a common shortcut and a common source of nuisance tripping afterwards.
  • Can you install the disposal itself, or just wire it? — Our scope is the electrical work — circuit, switch and protection. We coordinate with your plumber or fitter for the unit itself.
  • Does a disposal need GFCI protection? — Protection requirements around sinks are strict and this is exactly the sort of item an inspector looks at. We install to that standard as a matter of course.
  • I am remodelling the kitchen. What should I ask for? — Circuit count and panel capacity, before the cabinets. Retrofitting a circuit into a finished kitchen costs several times what it costs beforehand.
  • Is a permit needed? — Not usually for wiring an existing circuit. A new circuit generally is, and a full kitchen remodel definitely is.

Types of Homes in Chicago & Their Wiring::

What Chicago's building stock actually is

Cook County Assessor data makes the pattern unambiguous, and it explains most of what we find behind a cover plate.

83%

of properties in West Chicago township (Wicker Park, West Town, Ukrainian Village) predate 1940

1906

median year built in West Chicago township; 1908 in Lake View

265,194

masonry-walled properties citywide — why conduit through brick is routine here

306,261

properties with no central air — the load that gets added later

Why the age matters electrically

A building from 1906 was wired, if it was wired at all, for lighting. Everything since — the refrigerator, the window units, the home office, the induction range, the car — has been added to a service that was never designed for it. That is the single thread running through most Chicago electrical work.

Township by township

West Chicago is the oldest at 83% pre-1940 across 65,664 properties. Lake View follows at 71% across 23,046. Jefferson township — Portage Park, Jefferson Park, Irving Park — is younger at 60% pre-1940 but far larger at 112,923 properties, and its median year of 1927 puts most of it in the bungalow era. Rogers Park is the youngest of the north-side townships at a 1938 median.

What that means room by room

188,389 properties citywide are two-storey and 154,926 single-storey; 324,305 have full basements, which is where the panel usually lives and where access is usually straightforward. 107,336 properties have no garage at all — relevant the moment an EV charger enters the conversation. And 335,769 use a warm-air furnace against 98,849 on hot water or steam, which decides what kind of equipment circuits exist already.

What the permit record shows

Chicago publishes every permit it issues. That makes contractor claims checkable, including ours.

What we actually pull permits for

Our own job-type mix: 307 service or new service permits, 206 outlets and receptacles, 163 electrical panel, 162 200-amp service upgrades, 126 lighting, 117 100-amp service and 33 at 400 amp or larger. By permit route, 527 went through the Express Permit Program, 340 new construction and 325 renovation or alteration.

Where we work most

Ward 1 (129 permits), Ward 32 (85), Ward 26 (72), Ward 47 (68) and Ward 27 (63) lead our record — the north and northwest sides, consistent with a shop on N Lincoln Ave.

The citywide picture

Chicago issued 20,187 electrical permits in 24 months. Lighting leads at 9,748, outlets and receptacles at 9,306, service work at 6,672, panels at 5,219 and solar at 4,033. At the other end, rewires ran to 28 permits and ceiling fans to 3 — a useful corrective to any contractor telling you a whole-house rewire is routine.

One honest caveat

Permit values are the reported construction value of the whole project, which often includes trades other than ours. They are a good guide to the scale of a job and a poor guide to a contractor's revenue. We quote from scope, not from permit data.

Where we work, and what changes between areas

North Side — Lincoln Square, North Park, Albany Park, Ravenswood

Our home patch, minutes from the shop on N Lincoln Ave. Dense bungalow and two-flat stock; fuse boxes and 100A services still turn up regularly.

Lakefront — Uptown, Rogers Park, Lakeview

Lake View township is 71% pre-1940. Courtyard buildings and pre-war condo conversions, where metering and common-area circuits dominate.

Northwest — Logan Square, Wicker Park, Jefferson Park

West Chicago township is 83% pre-1940 — the oldest stock in the city. Knob-and-tube behind new drywall is the recurring surprise on rehab work.

Suburbs — Evanston and Palatine

Current registration in both (18LICL-0250 and CON-006592-2024), so we can pull permits there. Our DuPage registrations have lapsed and we do not sell permit-bearing work there.

Ward 1, 32, 26, 47 and 27 carry the largest share of our permit record, which is simply where a north-side shop ends up working.

||Electrical Repair Services — Detail::

Electrical Repair Services in Chicago — the practical detail

Half a house without power, a burning smell, a circuit that died overnight. Diagnosis is the entire job — everything after that is just parts — and in Chicago's pre-war stock the fault is rarely where the symptom is.

What drives the cost

Repair pricing is diagnosis-led by definition. The permit data below is the citywide context for the work that does get permitted.

Before you book anyone

  • There is a burning smell from an outlet. What should I do? — Stop using that circuit, switch it off at the panel if you can do so safely, and call. This is one of the few genuinely urgent electrical symptoms.
  • Half my house lost power but the breaker is fine. Why? — Frequently a lost phase or a failed connection at the panel or service. It is a real fault, it is not something to wait out, and it is a common call for us.
  • Do I need a whole rewire? — Almost certainly not. Chicago issued 28 rewire permits in 24 months across the entire city — it is genuinely rare. Most 'you need a rewire' quotes are one bad circuit.
  • Do you work weekends? — We do, and our reviewers mention it specifically. Saturday hours are 7:00am to 3:00pm.
  • What does knob-and-tube mean for my house? — It means live original wiring behind newer surfaces. It is not automatically an emergency, but it does change what can safely be added to those circuits.

||Electrical Panel & Service Upgrade — Detail::

Electrical Panel & Service Upgrade in Chicago — the practical detail

Chicago issued 5,219 panel permits and 2,863 200-amp service upgrades in the last 24 months. It is the most-permitted major work in the city, and it is the job where the difference between a competent contractor and a cheap one shows up at inspection.

What drives the cost

This is the category where Chicago's permit data is most reliable — thousands of costed permits rather than a handful. These are real reported values from real jobs across the city.

Before you book anyone

  • How do I know if I need a panel upgrade? — A full panel, a fuse box, breakers tripping under normal load, or a planned EV charger or central air. A load calculation answers it properly — spare breaker spaces do not.
  • How much does a 200-amp upgrade cost in Chicago? — Across 2,862 costed permits in 24 months the median reported construction value was $4,700. That is the citywide distribution, not a quote — yours depends on the meter, riser and service entrance.
  • How long is the power off? — Usually part of a single day, provided ComEd coordination is scheduled in advance. Poor scheduling is what turns this into a multi-day problem.
  • Do I need a permit? — Yes. Panel and service replacement is permitted, inspected work. We pull and close it in-house under ECC96456.
  • Is 200A always right? — No. It is the common target for a modern single-family home, but the correct size comes from the load calculation. Some buildings need more, some genuinely do not need it at all.

||Circuit Breaker Replacement & Repair — Detail::

Circuit Breaker Replacement & Repair in Chicago — the practical detail

A breaker that trips is telling you something, and it is not always that the breaker is bad. We diagnose the circuit before anyone quotes a panel — then, because we hold current City of Chicago registration, we pull and close the permit when the work needs one.

What drives the cost

We do not publish a flat-rate price book, because the same symptom can be a free reset or a service upgrade. What we can publish is the citywide permit data and exactly what drives the number.

Before you book anyone

  • My breaker keeps tripping. Does it need replacing? — Usually not. A breaker that trips is doing its job — something on that circuit is drawing more current than it should, or there is a fault. Replacing the breaker without finding the cause removes the warning and leaves the problem.
  • Do I need a permit for breaker work in Chicago? — Not for a repair or a like-for-like breaker replacement. You do for a panel replacement, a service upgrade, or in most cases adding a new circuit. We pull and close it in-house.
  • I have a Federal Pacific or Zinsco panel. Is it really a problem? — Yes, and it is one of the few cases where we recommend replacement without trying a repair first. Both have a documented history of breakers failing to trip under fault conditions.
  • Why can't you just add a breaker to my full panel? — Sometimes we can — tandem breakers fit certain panels. But spaces are not the real limit; service capacity is. That is why a load calculation comes before a price on any new circuit.
  • Will you come out for a single breaker? — Yes. It is the thing our reviewers mention most, because it is genuinely hard to find a Chicago electrician who will take one.

What Chicago's building stock actually is

Cook County Assessor data makes the pattern unambiguous, and it explains most of what we find behind a cover plate.

properties with no central air — the load that gets added later

Why the age matters electrically

A building from 1906 was wired, if it was wired at all, for lighting. Everything since — the refrigerator, the window units, the home office, the induction range, the car — has been added to a service that was never designed for it. That is the single thread running through most Chicago electrical work.

Township by township

West Chicago is the oldest at 83% pre-1940 across 65,664 properties. Lake View follows at 71% across 23,046. Jefferson township — Portage Park, Jefferson Park, Irving Park — is younger at 60% pre-1940 but far larger at 112,923 properties, and its median year of 1927 puts most of it in the bungalow era. Rogers Park is the youngest of the north-side townships at a 1938 median.

What that means room by room

188,389 properties citywide are two-storey and 154,926 single-storey; 324,305 have full basements, which is where the panel usually lives and where access is usually straightforward. 107,336 properties have no garage at all — relevant the moment an EV charger enters the conversation. And 335,769 use a warm-air furnace against 98,849 on hot water or steam, which decides what kind of equipment circuits exist already.

What we actually pull permits for

Our own job-type mix: 307 service or new service permits, 206 outlets and receptacles, 163 electrical panel, 162 200-amp service upgrades, 126 lighting, 117 100-amp service and 33 at 400 amp or larger. By permit route, 527 went through the Express Permit Program, 340 new construction and 325 renovation or alteration.

Where we work most

Ward 1 (129 permits), Ward 32 (85), Ward 26 (72), Ward 47 (68) and Ward 27 (63) lead our record — the north and northwest sides, consistent with a shop on N Lincoln Ave.

The citywide picture

Chicago issued 20,187 electrical permits in 24 months. Lighting leads at 9,748, outlets and receptacles at 9,306, service work at 6,672, panels at 5,219 and solar at 4,033. At the other end, rewires ran to 28 permits and ceiling fans to 3 — a useful corrective to any contractor telling you a whole-house rewire is routine.

One honest caveat

Permit values are the reported construction value of the whole project, which often includes trades other than ours. They are a good guide to the scale of a job and a poor guide to a contractor's revenue. We quote from scope, not from permit data.

||Outdoor & Security Lighting Installation — Detail::

Outdoor & Security Lighting Installation in Chicago — the practical detail

Outdoor lighting is a permitted electrical circuit before it is a design choice — a new fixture, a switch loop and weatherproof boxes rated for exterior use. Lighting is Chicago's single highest-volume electrical permit category, and outdoor work carries its own wet-location code requirements indoor lighting does not.

What drives the cost

Lighting is grouped as one broad permit category citywide, so the median reflects all lighting work, not outdoor fixtures specifically — still the best available anchor.

Before you book anyone

  • Do I need a permit for outdoor lighting? — Depends on the scope. Adding a fixture to an existing exterior circuit usually does not; running a new circuit through masonry generally does, and we pull it under ECC96456.
  • What makes exterior wiring different from indoor? — Every exterior receptacle requires GFCI protection, and every fixture and box needs a wet-location or damp-location rating. Interior-rated hardware fails inspection outdoors.
  • Can you add lighting to my garage or alley entry? — Yes, and it is one of our more common security-lighting calls — usually a motion-activated fixture on a new or existing circuit.
  • Do you install landscape or low-voltage lighting? — Yes, including the transformer and cable runs, alongside standard line-voltage exterior circuits.
  • How long does an outdoor lighting job take? — A straightforward fixture swap or addition is usually a single visit; a new circuit through masonry takes longer and depends on the run length.

||Tesla & EV Charger Installation — Detail::

Tesla & EV Charger Installation in Chicago — the practical detail

A Level 2 home charger is a dedicated 240V circuit, sized to your panel's actual spare capacity, before it is a Tesla or Rivian accessory. Chicago issued 825 EV charger permits in the last 24 months — real, permitted, growing volume, not a niche request.

What drives the cost

Chicago publishes reported construction value on every electrical permit. With 825 costed EV charger permits, this median is a reliable anchor.

Before you book anyone

  • Do I need a panel upgrade for an EV charger? — Often, but not always. It depends on your panel's spare capacity, which is why we calculate the actual load before recommending anything.
  • Can you run a charger to a detached garage? — Yes, and it is a common Chicago scenario given how many garages sit behind the house. The scope usually includes trenching or conduit for the run.
  • Is a permit required for a home EV charger? — Yes. It is inspected electrical work, and we pull and close the permit under ECC96456.
  • Do you install Tesla-specific equipment? — Yes, along with ChargePoint, JuiceBox and other major brands. We install customer-supplied chargers as standard.
  • How fast is Level 2 charging compared to a wall outlet? — Meaningfully faster — Level 2 charging is what makes an EV practical to charge overnight, which is the reason for a dedicated circuit rather than an extension cord to a standard outlet.

||Fire Alarm System Installation, Inspection & Testing — Detail::

Fire Alarm System Installation, Inspection and Testing in Chicago — the practical detail

A fire alarm system is inspected life-safety equipment, not a smoke detector you can swap yourself. Chicago issued 2,559 fire alarm permits in the last 24 months, and testing requirements do not stop once the system is installed.

What drives the cost

Chicago publishes reported construction value on every electrical permit. Fire alarm systems show real cost variation between residential interconnection and commercial monitored panels.

Before you book anyone

  • Do I need a permit for a fire alarm system? — Yes for new installation or significant modification. Testing and inspection of an existing system typically does not require a new permit. We pull and close installation permits under ECC96456.
  • How often does a fire alarm system need testing? — Annually as a baseline for most residential and commercial systems, sometimes more frequently depending on occupancy type.
  • What's the difference between a smoke detector and a fire alarm system? — A fire alarm system is a monitored, code-compliant network of devices reporting to a central panel — meaningfully more than interconnected smoke detectors, though both matter.
  • My system failed inspection. What now? — We diagnose what specifically failed — device placement, wiring, panel programming — and correct it rather than guessing at a full replacement.
  • Do you handle commercial monitoring connections? — Yes, including the central-station tie-in that commercial and multi-unit systems typically require.

Types of Homes in Chicago & Their Wiring::

What Chicago's building stock actually is

Cook County Assessor data makes the pattern unambiguous, and it explains most of what we find behind a cover plate.

83%

Why the age matters electrically

A building from 1906 was wired, if it was wired at all, for lighting. Everything since — the refrigerator, the window units, the home office, the induction range, the car — has been added to a service that was never designed for it. That is the single thread running through most Chicago electrical work.

Township by township

West Chicago is the oldest at 83% pre-1940 across 65,664 properties. Lake View follows at 71% across 23,046. Jefferson township — Portage Park, Jefferson Park, Irving Park — is younger at 60% pre-1940 but far larger at 112,923 properties, and its median year of 1927 puts most of it in the bungalow era. Rogers Park is the youngest of the north-side townships at a 1938 median.

What that means room by room

188,389 properties citywide are two-storey and 154,926 single-storey; 324,305 have full basements, which is where the panel usually lives and where access is usually straightforward. 107,336 properties have no garage at all — relevant the moment an EV charger enters the conversation. And 335,769 use a warm-air furnace against 98,849 on hot water or steam, which decides what kind of equipment circuits exist already.

By permit route, 527 went through the Express Permit Program, 340 new construction and 325 renovation or alteration.

||Electrical Outlet Installation & Repair — Detail::

Electrical Outlet Installation and Repair in Chicago — the practical detail

Outlets and receptacles are Chicago's second-highest-volume permitted electrical category — 9,306 permits in 24 months. Most calls are simple; the ones that aren't usually trace back to a circuit condition the outlet itself didn't cause.

What drives the cost

With 9,304 costed outlet permits, this is one of the most reliable medians in the dataset.

Before you book anyone

  • Do I need a permit to add an outlet? — Not always. A single outlet on an existing circuit typically does not need one; adding a new circuit generally does.
  • Why is my outlet dead but the breaker hasn't tripped? — Often a loose or failed connection somewhere upstream on the circuit — a backstabbed wire, a bad splice — rather than the outlet itself.
  • Can you add an outlet behind my TV without cutting drywall? — Usually yes, particularly on accessible walls. We assess access before quoting rather than after.
  • What's the difference between GFCI and AFCI protection? — GFCI protects against ground faults (common near water); AFCI protects against arc faults (common in bedroom and living space wiring). Many circuits now require both.
  • Is my outlet safe if it's ungrounded? — It can be made code-compliant with GFCI protection and correct labelling, which is common and legitimate in Chicago's pre-war housing stock.

||Recessed Lighting Installation — Detail::

Recessed Lighting Installation in Chicago — the practical detail

A recessed lighting project is judged on the ceiling afterward, not just whether the cans light up — clean spacing, patched drywall and a switch layout that actually matches how the room is used. Chicago condo and rehab projects routinely run to a dozen or more fixtures in a single visit.

What drives the cost

Lighting is one broad permit category citywide, so the reported median covers all lighting work rather than recessed fixtures alone — still the most reliable public anchor available.

Before you book anyone

  • How many recessed lights do I actually need? — It depends on ceiling height, fixture spacing and how the room is used — more fixtures spaced correctly beats fewer fixtures spaced arbitrarily. We lay this out before installation.
  • Can you retrofit cans into a finished ceiling without major drywall work? — Yes, remodel-rated fixtures are designed to fit through a cut opening in existing drywall.
  • Do I need a new circuit for recessed lighting? — Sometimes — it depends on how many fixtures are going in and what is already on the existing circuit. We check capacity before quoting.
  • Will my existing dimmer work with LED recessed lights? — Often not without swapping it — many older dimmers are not rated for LED loads and cause flickering. We confirm compatibility as part of the job.
  • Is a permit needed for recessed lighting? — Generally yes for new circuits or larger scopes; we pull and close it under ECC96456.

A whole-house rewire is one of the rarest things Chicago actually permits — 28 permits citywide in 24 months. Most 'you need a rewire' quotes are one bad circuit, and the diagnosis that tells the difference is the actual job.

What drives the cost

Whole-house rewiring is genuinely rare permitted work in Chicago — only 28 permits in 24 months, too few to publish a reliable median. Price follows the actual scope, not a citywide average.

Before you book anyone

  • Do I actually need a full rewire? — In our experience, almost never. Chicago issued 28 rewire permits citywide in 24 months, and most homes we are told 'need a rewire' turn out to have one problem circuit.
  • Is knob-and-tube wiring dangerous? — Not automatically, but it does change what can safely be added to those circuits and how insurance underwriters view the property. We assess the actual condition rather than assuming.
  • My renovation exposed old wiring. What now? — We assess what is actually there — age, condition, whether it is still in use — rather than assuming it all needs replacing because a wall is open.
  • Do I need a permit to rewire a single circuit? — Often not for a like-for-like repair; a new circuit or larger scope generally does, and we pull it when it applies.

Why the age matters electrically

A building from 1906 was wired, if it was wired at all, for lighting. Everything since — the refrigerator, the window units, the home office, the induction range, the car — has been added to a service that was never designed for it. That is the single thread running through most Chicago electrical work.

Township by township

West Chicago is the oldest at 83% pre-1940 across 65,664 properties. Lake View follows at 71% across 23,046. Jefferson township — Portage Park, Jefferson Park, Irving Park — is younger at 60% pre-1940 but far larger at 112,923 properties, and its median year of 1927 puts most of it in the bungalow era. Rogers Park is the youngest of the north-side townships at a 1938 median.

What that means room by room

188,389 properties citywide are two-storey and 154,926 single-storey; 324,305 have full basements, which is where the panel usually lives and where access is usually straightforward. 107,336 properties have no garage at all — relevant the moment an EV charger enters the conversation. And 335,769 use a warm-air furnace against 98,849 on hot water or steam, which decides what kind of equipment circuits exist already.

||Carbon Monoxide Detector Installation — Detail::

Carbon Monoxide Detector Installation in Chicago — the practical detail

CO detection is a separate legal requirement from smoke detection, not an add-on to it — and in a city with as much gas heat and as many older furnaces as Chicago, it is not optional in practice either. Hardwired, interconnected units are the code-compliant standard, not battery units bought at a hardware store.

What drives the cost

CO and smoke detector work is grouped as one small permit category citywide — 68 costed permits in 24 months, too few for a reliable median. Price follows device count and building layout instead.

Before you book anyone

  • Do I need a CO detector if I already have smoke detectors? — Yes — they are separate legal requirements. A combination unit can satisfy both, but a smoke-only detector does not cover CO.
  • How do I know if my CO detector has expired? — Check the manufacture date on the unit. CO sensors typically have a 5-10 year service life and stop reliably detecting gas after that, even if the alarm still powers on.
  • Are battery-only CO detectors compliant? — Requirements vary by building and situation; hardwired, interconnected detection is the more robust standard and what we install by default.
  • Can one CO detector cover my whole house? — Generally no for anything beyond a small single-level home — interconnected detection across levels and sleeping areas is the standard approach.
  • My CO detector keeps going off. Is that a false alarm? — Treat it as real until proven otherwise. We can inspect the unit and the likely CO sources, but do not ignore a repeating alarm.

||Landscape & Garden Lighting Installation — Detail::

Landscape & Garden Lighting Installation in Chicago — the practical detail

Landscape lighting is layered low-voltage electrical work — a transformer, buried cable and fixtures sized for the effect, not a string of stake lights from a hardware store. Getting the layering right is the difference between a lit yard and a floodlit one.

What drives the cost

Landscape lighting is grouped inside Chicago's broad lighting permit category, so the citywide median reflects all lighting work rather than low-voltage garden systems specifically.

Before you book anyone

  • How much landscape lighting does my yard actually need? — Fewer, well-placed fixtures layered for path, accent and uplighting usually look better and cost less than flooding the whole property. We design to the property, not a fixture count.
  • My landscape lighting stopped working in one area. Do I need to re-dig everything? — Usually not — a dead zone is most often one bad connection or a nicked cable, which we trace before recommending a full re-run.
  • Is landscape lighting a DIY-friendly project? — Low-voltage systems are safer than line-voltage work, but layout, cable burial depth and transformer sizing are where amateur installs commonly go wrong.
  • Can you add to a system I already have? — Yes, provided the existing transformer has spare capacity — we check that before proposing additions.
  • Do you do both design and installation? — Yes, and it is worth doing together — a layout designed for the property looks materially different from lights placed evenly around the perimeter.

  • Why do my smoke detectors need to be interconnected? — So that one triggering alarm sounds throughout the building, not just in the room where the smoke is — critical for anyone asleep elsewhere in the home.
  • How do I know if my smoke detector has expired? — Check the manufacture date on the unit. Most smoke sensors have about a 10-year service life regardless of whether the alarm still powers on.
  • My detector chirps every few minutes. Is that urgent? — Usually a low battery or end-of-life sensor rather than a wiring fault, but a chirping detector should be addressed promptly rather than muted or removed.
  • Can you interconnect detectors that are currently standalone? — Yes, this is a common retrofit in older buildings that were never wired for interconnection.

What Chicago's building stock actually is

Cook County Assessor data makes the pattern unambiguous, and it explains most of what we find behind a cover plate.

Why the age matters electrically

A building from 1906 was wired, if it was wired at all, for lighting. Everything since — the refrigerator, the window units, the home office, the induction range, the car — has been added to a service that was never designed for it. That is the single thread running through most Chicago electrical work.

Township by township

West Chicago is the oldest at 83% pre-1940 across 65,664 properties. Lake View follows at 71% across 23,046. Jefferson township — Portage Park, Jefferson Park, Irving Park — is younger at 60% pre-1940 but far larger at 112,923 properties, and its median year of 1927 puts most of it in the bungalow era. Rogers Park is the youngest of the north-side townships at a 1938 median.

What that means room by room

188,389 properties citywide are two-storey and 154,926 single-storey; 324,305 have full basements, which is where the panel usually lives and where access is usually straightforward. 107,336 properties have no garage at all — relevant the moment an EV charger enters the conversation. And 335,769 use a warm-air furnace against 98,849 on hot water or steam, which decides what kind of equipment circuits exist already.

By permit route, 527 went through the Express Permit Program, 340 new construction and 325 renovation or alteration.

Where we work most

Ward 1 (129 permits), Ward 32 (85), Ward 26 (72), Ward 47 (68) and Ward 27 (63) lead our record — the north and northwest sides, consistent with a shop on N Lincoln Ave.

The citywide picture

Chicago issued 20,187 electrical permits in 24 months. Lighting leads at 9,748, outlets and receptacles at 9,306, service work at 6,672, panels at 5,219 and solar at 4,033. ||Home & Commercial Energy Audit — Detail::

Home & Commercial Energy Audit in Chicago — the practical detail

An energy audit is not itself permitted electrical work — it is the assessment that tells you which electrical and mechanical upgrades are actually worth doing, before you spend on any of them. In Chicago's older housing stock, that assessment routinely turns up an electrical capacity issue before an efficiency one.

What drives the cost

An energy audit is not itself permitted electrical work, so there is no City of Chicago permit median for it. Price follows building size and assessment depth.

Before you book anyone

  • Do I need an energy audit before going solar? — It is not legally required, but it is the fastest way to find out if your panel has spare capacity before you commit to a solar quote — and panel capacity is a very common constraint in Chicago's older stock.
  • Is an energy audit itself permitted work? — No. It is an assessment, not construction, so there is no City of Chicago permit or fee for the audit itself.
  • What's different about an electrician doing my energy audit versus a general auditor? — Most home-performance auditors are not licensed electricians. We assess electrical capacity the same way we would before quoting a panel upgrade or generator install — with an actual load calculation.
  • Will you try to sell me work based on the audit findings? — The assessment and any resulting installation are separate decisions. We tell you what we found; what you do with it, and who does it, is yours to decide.
  • Do you audit commercial or multi-unit buildings? — Yes, including buildings with multiple meters or shared electrical infrastructure.

||Structured & Network Cabling Installation — Detail::

Structured & Network Cabling Installation in Chicago — the practical detail

Structured cabling is the physical network most of a building's technology depends on — Ethernet runs, patch panels and termination done to a standard that supports whatever gets plugged in next, not just what's needed today. Low voltage and data cabling accounts for 2,074 Chicago permits in 24 months.

What drives the cost

With 2,071 costed low-voltage and data cabling permits, this is a reliable citywide median.

Before you book anyone

  • Do I need a permit for structured cabling? — Depends on scope — a few added drops usually don't, a full building cabling project alongside electrical work usually does. We assess and pull it when it applies.
  • What's the difference between Cat5e, Cat6 and Cat6A? — Bandwidth and distance capacity, increasing in that order. We size to your actual network needs rather than defaulting to the newest standard.
  • Can you add network drops to my existing office without disrupting work? — Yes, this is scheduled around your business hours as standard, not treated as an afterthought.
  • Do you test every cable run? — Yes — an untested run is a guess, not a finished job.
  • Do you install fiber as well as copper? — Yes, including building-to-building and floor-to-floor fiber backbone runs.

||Breaker Box & Panel Replacement — Detail::

Breaker Box & Panel Replacement in Chicago — the practical detail

A breaker box or panel showing its age — rust, a burning smell, breakers that won't stay seated — is not always a full service upgrade. Sometimes the panel itself needs replacing at the same amperage; sometimes it's the moment to upsize. Electrical panel work is one of Chicago's most-permitted categories, at 5,219 permits in 24 months.

What drives the cost

With 5,187 costed electrical panel permits, this is one of the most reliable medians in the whole dataset.

Before you book anyone

  • My panel looks rusted — does it need full replacement? — Not automatically. Surface corrosion and internal damage are different problems; we assess the actual condition before recommending a full swap.
  • I have a Federal Pacific or Zinsco panel — is that urgent? — It's one of the few cases where we recommend replacement over repair without hesitation. Both have a documented history of breakers failing to trip under fault.
  • Can you replace my panel at the same amperage rather than upgrading? — Yes — a like-for-like replacement is common when the existing service size is genuinely adequate.
  • Will my insurance require a specific panel brand? — Some insurers flag Federal Pacific and Zinsco specifically; we can provide documentation of replacement for your insurer if needed.
  • How long does a panel replacement take? — Usually part of a single day, with power off only during the swap itself.

Electrical Troubleshooting & Fault Finding in Chicago — the practical detail

An intermittent fault — lights that flicker only sometimes, an outlet that works some days and not others — is harder to find than an outright failure, and it's exactly the kind of job where a systematic approach beats a guess. Diagnosis is the entire job here; everything after it is just parts.

What drives the cost

Troubleshooting is diagnosis-led work and is rarely separately permitted. The citywide figure below is general context, not a category-specific median.

Before you book anyone

  • Do I need to know what's wrong before I call? — No — describing the symptom (when it happens, what triggers it) is enough for us to start. Diagnosis is the service.

  • How long does troubleshooting take? — Depends on the fault — straightforward issues resolve quickly, intermittent ones can take longer to reproduce and isolate.
  • Will you fix the problem in the same visit? — Often yes, once diagnosed. Some faults require a parts order or a larger scope we'll quote before proceeding.

Low Voltage Wiring & Installation in Chicago — the practical detail

Low voltage covers more than networking — doorbells, sensors, thermostats, control wiring and anything running below standard household voltage. It's a genuinely broad category, and most of it still benefits from being run and terminated by someone who does electrical work for a living.

Before you book anyone

||Energy Star Appliance Circuits — Detail::

Energy Star Appliance Circuits in Chicago — the practical detail

Energy Star appliances often draw power differently than what they're replacing — an induction range, a heat-pump water heater, or a high-efficiency HVAC unit can need a different circuit entirely, not just a plug swap. Getting the electrical side right is what actually delivers the efficiency gain.

What drives the cost

Appliance circuits aren't a distinct City of Chicago permit category on their own — they're typically filed under general electrical or panel work. Price follows the specific appliance and circuit requirement.

Before you book anyone

  • Does my Energy Star appliance need a different circuit than the old one? — Often yes — induction ranges, heat pump water heaters and high-efficiency HVAC equipment frequently have different load profiles than standard equipment.
  • Will an Energy Star appliance work on my existing wiring? — Sometimes, but not always. We assess the actual appliance specifications before assuming the existing circuit is adequate.
  • Do you sell the appliances? — No, our scope is the electrical work. We wire for whatever appliance you've purchased or are planning to purchase.
  • Is a permit needed for an appliance circuit? — Depends on scope — a straightforward dedicated circuit may not need one, larger panel work generally does.
  • Can you check my panel capacity before I buy a new appliance? — Yes, and it's worth doing before you commit to a purchase that needs more capacity than your panel has.

||Light Switch Installation & Replacement — Detail::

Light Switch Installation & Replacement in Chicago — the practical detail

A switch that doesn't work, sparks, or feels loose is usually a quick fix — but in Chicago's older housing stock, the wiring behind it is sometimes the actual story, not the switch itself.

What drives the cost

Switch work isn't a distinct City of Chicago permit category — it's typically grouped with outlets and receptacles. Price follows device type and wiring condition.

Before you book anyone

  • My switch sparked once. Is that dangerous? — Worth having checked promptly — it can be the device itself or a loose connection behind it, and the second one matters more.
  • Can you install a smart switch on my existing wiring? — Often yes, though many smart switches need a neutral wire that older circuits may not have. We check before installing.
  • Do you install dimmer switches for LED fixtures? — Yes, matched to the fixture's actual load type — not every dimmer works correctly with every LED fixture.
  • What's a three-way switch? — Two switches controlling one fixture from different locations — common at either end of a hallway or staircase.
  • Is a permit needed to replace a switch? — Generally not for a like-for-like replacement; adding a new circuit is different.
